query: Taken together, these findings establish the Mongolian gerbil as a useful model organism for studying the neurobiology of vocal interactions in complex social groups.

query: Four ultrasonic microphones (Avisoft CM16/CMPA48AAF-5V) were synchronously recorded using a National Instruments multifunction data acquisition device (PCI-6143) via BNC connection with a National Instruments terminal block (BNC-2110). The recording was controlled with custom python scripts using the NI-DAQmx-python library version 0.5.7; (https://github.com/ni/nidaqmx-python; National Instruments, 2017) which wrote samples to disk at a 125 kHz sampling rate.

query: Audio was segmented by amplitude thresholding using the Autoencoded Vocal Analysis (AVA) python package (see Goffinet et al., 2021).

query: We quantified the false positive vocalization rate for each threshold value and selected 0.3, which had a 5.5+/-1.96% false positive rate.

query: A VAE was trained for 50 epochs using a model precision of 40.

query: GMMs were fit to cluster VAE latent feature vectors. To reduce computation time, we fit the model on 7 of 32 VAE latents (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), as these explained 99.5% of the variance in the original feature space.
matched_segment: GMMs were fit to cluster VAE latent feature vectors. To reduce computation time, we fit the model on 7 of 32 VAE latents (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), as these explained 99.5% of the variance in the original feature space.

query: The model was implemented in Stan (https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanpy), however similar clustering results were achieved using the scikit-learn Gaussian Mixture model class with a diagonal covariance matrix (https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.mixture.GaussianMixture.html). We fit the model using stochastic variational inference, an approximate Bayesian inference technique that recasts the task of learning a posterior distribution as an optimization problem and enables vast speedups (Hoffman et al., 2013).

We fit the model using stochastic variational inference, an approximate Bayesian inference technique that recasts the task of learning a posterior distribution as an optimization problem and enables vast speedups (Hoffman et al., 2013).

query: GMMs typically assume that the whole population selects clusters with the same probabilities, however we modified this assumption to allow, although not enforce, the model to learn different cluster usage patterns for each family.
